children: Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy puts a spotlight on governance at the $4.5 trln chipmaker he leads, with fallout for customers from Anthropic to Alibaba. The distraction may help rival Huawei but Beijing has more to lose if Washington tightens export controls.
Full view will be published shortly.

Nvidia's board of directors on November 8 said it is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent media reporting on whether its founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

On the same day, Huang apologised for being unfaithful to his wife and said he was committed to winning back the confidence of Nvidia's board, partners and shareholders. The company added that he is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption.

On November 6, the Financial Times reported that the US believed Huang had a romantic relationship with a Chinese woman who was recruited to spy for China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. American officials this year wrote a memo, based on information from US intelligence, which said the Nvidia boss had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, who was at the time an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer, the FT report added, citing people familiar with the document.
Alice Huang is not related to Jensen Huang. China’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

In late October, the New York Times reported that American officials had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset and had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang, citing sources. A year earlier, the publication reported that US Commerce Department officials had been investigating Megaspeed for helping Chinese companies sidestep American export restrictions, citing sources.
Nvidia's CEO told Bloomberg News last month that his relationship and interactions with Alice Huang were related to Megaspeed and were "completely normal and not unusual".
